summary: Defines an extension to the Atom Syndication Format for describing the licenses associated with feeds and entries. It is an experimental protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: A news feed can say what you are allowed to do with its stories. This extension adds that permission label.

questions: how to add a license to an atom feed
what is the atom license extension
how do atom entries inherit licenses
what is the difference between atom:rights and a license link
subtitle: Adding licensing information to feeds and individual entries

tldr.problem: Feed publishers want to tell readers what they are allowed to do with syndicated content, but the Atom Syndication Format has no standard way to attach machine-readable licensing information.
tldr.mechanism: The license extension adds a "license" link relation that can be included in Atom feeds and entries. Each link points to a license resource that can be human-readable, machine-readable, or both.
tldr.outcome: Feeds can now describe their licensing terms, though the extension remains experimental because feed consumers rarely use the metadata yet.

today: RFC 4946 is an Experimental RFC that has not been obsoleted. The extension is technically available for use in Atom feeds, but adoption among feed consumers remains limited.

sections.title: Adding License Information to Atom
sections.content:
The Atom Syndication Format is a standard way for publishers to describe feeds of content and entries. This extension adds the ability to declare what licenses apply to a feed or individual entries within it.

Publishers already use Atom to syndicate blogs, news, and other content. While it is common practice for publishers to say what license applies, there was no standard way to attach this information in a way both humans and software could understand. This specification fills that gap by defining a "license" link relation.
sections.plainLanguage: An Atom feed is like a news stand that pushes out stories. This extension lets the stand post a license sign that says what people can do with those stories.

sections.title: The License Link Relation
sections.content:
The "license" link relation can appear in feed or entry elements. A feed or entry may contain multiple license links (for dual-licensed content), but each must have a unique combination of href and type attributes.

The href attribute points to a resource that describes the license. This could be a web page, an RDF file, or any other format. When multiple licenses are specified, each should include a title attribute with a human-readable label to distinguish them. If an entry declares any license (including an unspecified one), it does not inherit licenses from its containing feed.

The RFC defines a special unspecified license link (with href equal to "http://purl.org/atompub/license#unspecified") to indicate that no specific license has been assigned. An entry using this must not contain any other license links.
sections.plainLanguage: The license link is like a tag on a story that points to a document saying what you can do with it. If a story has its own license tag, it overrides the feed's general license.

sections.title: Inheritance and Relationship to atom:rights
sections.content:
Atom entries can inherit licenses from their containing feed. More specifically, if an entry has no license links, it inherits the feed's licenses. However, if an atom:source element is present in the entry, the entry inherits from the source instead of the feed. This allows entries copied from one feed to another to preserve their original licensing.

The license link relation differs from Atom's atom:rights element. The atom:rights element is meant to be human-readable copyright or rights statements, while the "license" link is meant to provide machine-readable licensing information. Both can coexist, and they should be consistent with each other to avoid confusion about what rights are actually granted.
sections.plainLanguage: If a story does not have its own license, it gets the license from the feed it comes from. The license link is different from a copyright notice—it is meant for computers to read, not just people.

sections.title: Deployment and Security
sections.content:
The license extension is described as experimental in the RFC because, at the time of publication, very few feed consumers actually used license metadata. While it is common practice for feed publishers to declare licenses, widespread support for consuming and interpreting this data was still uncertain.

When implementing license links, follow the same security considerations as for any links in Atom documents, as specified in the main Atom specification. Implementations should properly resolve relative URI references using the xml:base attribute when present.
sections.plainLanguage: This extension is still being tested because most feed readers do not yet pay attention to license information. Implementers should be careful about how they resolve web addresses and follow general security practices for links.
